Wolfe Tone.fact: Six days before, Tone had embarked with Admiral Jean-Baptiste-François Bompart and General Jean Hardy in command of a force of about 3,000 men. Tone, on the ship Hoche, refused Bompart's offer of escape in a frigate.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In the ensuing battle of _____ he commanded one of the ship's batteries until, isolated and crippled after several hours of bombardment, the ship struck and Bompart surrendered
Wolfe Tone.fact: In the ensuing battle of Tory Island he commanded one of the ship's batteries until, isolated and crippled after several hours of bombardment, the ship struck and Bompart surrendered.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: I entered into the service of the _____ with the sole view of being useful to my country
Wolfe Tone.fact: I entered into the service of the French Republic with the sole view of being useful to my country.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In such enterprises, everything depends on success: _____ succeeded – Kosciusko failed
Wolfe Tone.fact: In such enterprises, everything depends on success: Washington succeeded – Kosciusko failed.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: His one request was that, as a ranking _____ officer, he might "die the death of a soldier" and be shot
Wolfe Tone.fact: His one request was that, as a ranking French officer, he might "die the death of a soldier" and be shot.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: Theobald Wolfe Tone died on 19 November _____ at the age of 35 in the Provost Prison of the Royal Barracks, Dublin, not far from where he was born
Wolfe Tone.fact: Theobald Wolfe Tone died on 19 November 1798 at the age of 35 in the Provost Prison of the Royal Barracks, Dublin, not far from where he was born.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: He is buried in the family plot in Bodenstown, _____, near his birthplace at Sallins, and his grave is in the care of the National Graves Association
Wolfe Tone.fact: He is buried in the family plot in Bodenstown, County Kildare, near his birthplace at Sallins, and his grave is in the care of the National Graves Association.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In the autobiography he began to compose in France, Tone claimed that already in _____ he had advanced "the question of separation with scarcely any reserve"
Wolfe Tone.fact: In the autobiography he began to compose in France, Tone claimed that already in 1790 he had advanced "the question of separation with scarcely any reserve". While not yet rejecting a personal union of crowns, in his tract The Spanish War (1790) he had disputed Ireland's obligation to support Britain in the Nootka Crisis with Spain and had called for a separate Irish navy.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: In the autobiography he began to compose in France, Tone claimed that already in 1790 he had advanced "the question of separation with scarcely any reserve". While not yet rejecting a personal union of crowns, in his tract The Spanish War (1790) he had disputed Ireland's obligation to support Britain in the Nootka Crisis with Spain and had called for a separate Irish navy.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: He is also recorded as telling the French that a revolution in _____ "was not to be made for the people of property"
Wolfe Tone.fact: While not yet rejecting a personal union of crowns, in his tract The Spanish War (1790) he had disputed Ireland's obligation to support Britain in the Nootka Crisis with Spain and had called for a separate Irish navy. He is also recorded as telling the French that a revolution in Ireland "was not to be made for the people of property".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: Russell's diary records a despondent conversation in January _____ in which Tone remarked: there is "nothing to be expected from this country except from the sans culottes, who are too ignorant for an
Wolfe Tone.fact: Russell's diary records a despondent conversation in January 1794 in which Tone remarked: there is "nothing to be expected from this country except from the sans culottes, who are too ignorant for any thinking man to wish to see in power".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: Tone did not abandon _____ constitutionalism, so long as the talk was of reform
Wolfe Tone.fact: Tone did not abandon Whig constitutionalism, so long as the talk was of reform.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In _____, in an address to Volunteers, he disclaimed any intention of invading the "just prerogatives of our monarch" or the "constitutional powers of the peers of the realm"
Wolfe Tone.fact: In 1792, in an address to Volunteers, he disclaimed any intention of invading the "just prerogatives of our monarch" or the "constitutional powers of the peers of the realm".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: As a condition of _____ emancipation he had even offered that the greater part of a non-confessional Irish electorate be disenfranchised
Wolfe Tone.fact: As a condition of Catholic emancipation he had even offered that the greater part of a non-confessional Irish electorate be disenfranchised. Anticipating the terms under which Catholics were eventually admitted to a United Kingdom parliament in 1829, his Argument proposed raising the property (or tenure equivalent) threshold for the vote fivefold to match the English ten-pound freehold.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: Even when set on an insurrectionary path, Tone expressed no wish to unsettle property in _____
Wolfe Tone.fact: Even when set on an insurrectionary path, Tone expressed no wish to unsettle property in Ireland.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: This he would hope to avoid, for not only would he abhor the bloodshed, but he believed that the prospect of retaining property in _____ might blunt resistance
Wolfe Tone.fact: Even when set on an insurrectionary path, Tone expressed no wish to unsettle property in Ireland. This he would hope to avoid, for not only would he abhor the bloodshed, but he believed that the prospect of retaining property in Ireland might blunt resistance.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: Tone approved the advance of peasant proprietorship under the _____, and may broadly have shared Jefferson's faith in the republican virtues of independent smallholders
Wolfe Tone.fact: Tone approved the advance of peasant proprietorship under the French Republic, and may broadly have shared Jefferson's faith in the republican virtues of independent smallholders.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: But he insisted that the _____ society he had known in Ireland had never "entertained" ideas of "a distribution of property and an agrarian law", and he advanced no such scheme himself
Wolfe Tone.fact: But he insisted that the United society he had known in Ireland had never "entertained" ideas of "a distribution of property and an agrarian law", and he advanced no such scheme himself. In general, Tone appears to have followed the resolve of the Dublin Society of United Irishmen to "attend those things in which we all agree, [and] to exclude those in which we differ", and consequently to avoid directly engaging questions of economic inequality.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: From France, he wrote tracts addressed to the weavers of the _____ in Dublin
Wolfe Tone.fact: From France, he wrote tracts addressed to the weavers of the Liberties in Dublin. but James Hope, the self-educated weaver who organised in the Liberties, did not place Tone alongside his friend Russell as one of those "few" United Irish leaders who "perfectly" understood the real causes of social disorder: "the conditions of the labouring class".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: As was the case with the _____ society, Tone proposed an independent and representative government as a sufficient promise of redress regardless of the grievance
Wolfe Tone.fact: From France, he wrote tracts addressed to the weavers of the Liberties in Dublin. As was the case with the Dublin society, Tone proposed an independent and representative government as a sufficient promise of redress regardless of the grievance.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: It is matter of speculation as to what Tone, who prided himself on being a political pragmatist, would have found expedient in an _____ republic
Wolfe Tone.fact: but James Hope, the self-educated weaver who organised in the Liberties, did not place Tone alongside his friend Russell as one of those "few" United Irish leaders who "perfectly" understood the real causes of social disorder: "the conditions of the labouring class". For Tone, the promise appears to have been not, scarcely conceptualised, agrarian or labour reform, but the promotion of education (Tone imagined the polymath Whitley Stokes as the head of a national system) and a vigorous mercan...

Wolfe Tone.fact: Four years later when, believing that "the people of Ireland were in general very ignorant", General Clarke asked whether "we might choose a king", Tone's response was notably pragmatic.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: The only person with the least chance of fulfilling such a role, in Tone's view, was Lord Moira (after whom Tone had named his fourth child Francis Rawdon Tone).

Wolfe Tone.fact: But the Patriot aristocrat had "blown his reputation to pieces by accepting a command against France".

Wolfe Tone.fact: Tone's larger objection to an Irish crown was that the Dissenters, who he was in no doubt would "direct the public sentiment in framing a government", were "thoroughly enlightened and sincere republicans".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: He thought it "absurd" to suggest, as Clarke had done in his instructions to Hoche, that a member of the House of Stuart could be found who would be agreeable to all parties.

Wolfe Tone.fact: Tone had again to rebuff the suggestion of a Jacobite restoration—that the Catholic Pretender, Henry Benedict Stuart, be recognised as Henry IX, King of the Irish.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: But set upon a constitutional path by Daniel O'Connell, nationalist opinion in Ireland was slow to embrace his memory.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: Despite the efforts of his wife Mathilda and their son William who had collected his papers in a two-volume Life of Theobald Wolfe Tone (Washington in 1826), in the decades after his death, Tone's name languished in relative obscurity.

Wolfe Tone.fact: In his History of Ireland (1864), Mitchel drew uncritically from the Life, beginning what historian James Quinn suggests is a "long tradition in nationalist historiography of treating Tone's writing as sacred scripture".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: But while Tone many have been an "apostle" for those who rallied to the republic proclaimed by Pearse, Clarke and Connolly in 1916, writers with influence in the new Irish state after 1922 dismissed him as not being Irish enough.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In October 1798, on his second attempt to land in _____ with French troops and supplies, he was taken prisoner
Wolfe Tone.fact: Convinced that if his fellow Protestants feared to make common cause with the Catholic majority, the British Crown would continue to govern Ireland in the English interest, he helped form the Society of United Irishmen in 1791. In October 1798, on his second attempt to land in Ireland with French troops and supplies, he was taken prisoner.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: Tone, nonetheless, was baptised a Protestant, with the name Theobald Wolfe in honour of his godfather, Theobald Wolfe of Blackhall, County Kildare, a first cousin of Arthur Wolfe, 1st Viscount Kilwarden. In 1783, Tone found work as a tutor in the home of Richard Martin, a Patriot member of the Irish Parliament for Jamestown, County Leitrim.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In January 1793, Tone was included in the _____ delegation that, after being hosted by Presbyterian supporters in Belfast, was received by George III at Windsor
Wolfe Tone.fact: In December 1792, with the support and participation of United Irishmen, Tone helped the Committee in Dublin stage a national Catholic Convention. The impression was confirmed when the convention decided to make its appeal directly to London where the government, in advance of war with revolutionary France, had signalled a willingness to solicit Catholic opinion.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: But there was a substantial price to be paid for the passage, in April 1793, of similar legislation in _____
Wolfe Tone.fact: But there was a substantial price to be paid for the passage, in April 1793, of similar legislation in Ireland.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In the wake of the 1793 _____, the Catholic Committee voted Tone a sum of £1,500 with a gold medal, subscribed to a statue of the King and, as agreed in London, voted to dissolve
Wolfe Tone.fact: Through its appointed Dublin Castle executive, the British government pressed the Irish Parliament to match Westminster's 1791 Catholic Relief Act. In the wake of the 1793 Relief Act, the Catholic Committee voted Tone a sum of £1,500 with a gold medal, subscribed to a statue of the King and, as agreed in London, voted to dissolve.

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations
Wolfe Tone.question: In April 1794 _____ was arrested on a charge of treason and dramatically committed suicide during his trial
Wolfe Tone.fact: An Anglican clergyman radicalised by his experience of revolutionary Paris, Jackson came to Ireland to ascertain to the potential support for a French invasion. Tone had drawn up a memorandum for Jackson testifying to the readiness of the country to rise, the Presbyterians being "steady republicans, devoted to liberty" and the Catholics "ready for any change because no change can make them worse".

Wolfe Tone.subject: International Relations

Wolfe Tone.fact: The work by Edward Delaney was unveiled in 1967 by Éamon de Valera.

Wolfe Tone.fact: The work by Edward Delaney was unveiled in 1967 by Éamon de Valera.

Wolfe Tone.fact: In 1998, the rebellion's bicentenary, Sinn Féin president Gerry Adams and Taoiseach, Bertie Ahern made separate appearances at Bodenstown to claim Tone's sanction for their endorsement of the "Good Friday" Belfast Agreement.
